key_insight: Mapping free-boundary PDEs to an equivalent fixed-domain representation via topological conjugacy enables neural operators to learn and predict moving-boundary dynamics accurately and efficiently.
problem_solved: Neural operators struggle to represent PDEs with evolving (free) boundaries—common in problems like glacier melt—because the domain changes in time and breaks standard operator assumptions. This work provides a principled way to handle moving domains so operators can generalize and remain data-efficient.
method: Construct a topological-conjugacy transformation that maps the original free-boundary problem to a fixed reference domain while preserving the dynamical structure.
Train a neural operator (e.g., DeepONet/FNO-style architecture) on the transformed fixed-domain PDE to learn the solution operator and boundary evolution jointly.
Invert the transformation to recover predictions on the original moving domain, enabling accurate reconstruction of both field values and boundary motion.
impact: Enables scalable, generalizable operator-learning surrogates for moving-boundary physical systems (e.g., glacier dynamics, combustion fronts), improving prediction speed and data efficiency for scientific ML and climate applications.
